label: Dreischulte 70: Full blood count more than 8 weeks ago during auranofin treatment
title: No full blood count in the eight weeks up to an auranofin supply
statement: Patient treated with auranofin - had no FBC check in the last 8 weeks

plain_summary: The 2012 criterion flags a confirmed absence of a full blood count on the auranofin supply date and in the preceding eight weeks, including at the start of treatment. Australian guidance differs: the Australian tablet product information specifies a monthly full blood count including differential and platelets (Ridaura, section 4.4), and the Canadian capsule supplied under temporary Australian approval requires blood counts every two weeks for the first three months and at least monthly thereafter (Xediton, 2010).

needs_facts.what: Full blood count on the auranofin supply date under review or in the preceding 56 days
needs_facts.meets: The pharmacist or a checked test history confirms that no full blood count was completed on the specified supply date or in the preceding 56 days. A completed count anywhere in that interval closes the check. An unavailable result or an answer about a different supply leaves the check open.

options.words: Confirmed no count in that period

rule_for_models: Assess current or starting treatment at the latest Group A auranofin supply. A full blood count collected on that date or 1 to 56 days earlier gives no finding. Use the collection date on the test or verified pathology line. For current or starting treatment, report a finding only if the pharmacist or a verified test history confirms that no count was completed in that period. Cite the supply and the evidence confirming the gap, including a verified history of never having a count. If current use or testing is uncertain, cite the supply, report a possible finding and ask for the missing information. Use a pharmacist’s answer about a 56-day period only for the supply it covers.
cannot_be_seen: A pharmacy record can omit tests done elsewhere. An old report alone cannot establish the latest test date. A test order does not show that blood was collected. A first supply alone cannot establish the treatment period.
ask_the_gp: Could we confirm the latest completed full blood count and review the monitoring interval appropriate for this person's auranofin treatment?
